title: Frozen source-level boundary extraction for the first lineara JavaScript Map array

parent_parser.reason: The literal transform itself passed synthetic canaries, but the old source extractor used rfind(');') and captured later JavaScript Maps, producing Extra data after the first valid top-level array.

steps: Locate the literal marker new Map( selected by the source-specific adapter contract.
Advance over whitespace only and require the first argument character to be [.
Scan the original source left-to-right without executing JavaScript, tracking double-quoted string state and backslash escaping.
Outside strings, increment square-bracket depth on [ and decrement on ].
The payload ends at the first ] that returns the initial array depth from 1 to 0.
After that closing ], advance over whitespace only and require the exact source terminator );.
Extract only the original source substring from the initial [ through its matching top-level ].
Apply the separately frozen JANUS-JS-LITERAL-SUBSET-v0.2 normalization only to that extracted payload, then require strict JSON parsing.
frozen_boundary_algorithm.string_rule: Inside a double-quoted string, a backslash consumes the following source character for quote-boundary purposes; brackets inside strings never affect structural depth.

validation_canaries: A synthetic first Map followed by a second Map must return only the first Map array.
A string containing the characters ]); must not terminate the payload.
Escaped quotes inside source strings must not alter structural depth.
The exact characters after the matching top-level ] must be ); modulo whitespace.
Historical and current frozen lineara sources must both parse through the same boundary scanner and the same v0.2 literal transform.
Historical source identity must remain exactly 1609122 bytes / SHA-256 b7b383b93db55b504eb00c552a8b18c19a588e83bba7ff0ab93ca32277d8bfe2.
